ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AM=AC$, $BN=BC$. When $\angle A=30^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle MCN$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle A=30^\circ$ and $AC=AM$,\\
it follows that $\angle AMC=\frac{1}{2}\times \left(180^\circ-30^\circ\right)=75^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle B=60^\circ$ and $BC=BN$,\\
it implies $\angle CNB=\frac{1}{2}\times \left(180^\circ-60^\circ\right)=60^\circ$,\\
Thus, $\angle MCN=180^\circ-60^\circ-75^\circ=\boxed{45^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, C is at the lower left, B is at the upper left, and A is at the lower right; CB is vertical, CA is horizontal, and a right-angle mark is drawn at C, so ∠ACB=90°. Side BA is the hypotenuse, points M and N are both marked on the hypotenuse BA, and C is connected to M and N respectively; rays CM and CN are located inside the right angle ∠ACB. Reasoning: It is known that ∠A=30°, and ∠ACB=90°, so in right triangle ABC, ∠B=180°−90°−30°=60°. Because M is on BA, ∠CAM=∠CAB=30°. Also AM=AC, therefore triangle ACM is an isosceles triangle with A as the vertex angle, and the base angles ∠ACM=∠AMC=(180°−30°)/2=75°. Because N is on BA, ∠CBN=∠CBA=60°. Also BN=BC, therefore triangle BCN is an isosceles triangle with B as the vertex angle, and the base angles ∠BCN=∠CNB=(180°−60°)/2=60°. Since ∠ACB=90°, it can be obtained that ∠ACN=90°−∠BCN=90°−60°=30°. Thus ∠MCN=∠ACM−∠ACN=75°−30°=45°. Final answer: 45°.
